problems.quote: This formula explains why a heavier object requires more force to move at the same speed as a lighter one.
problems.problem: Newton's Second Law (F=ma) relates force to acceleration, not speed. A heavier object requires more force to *accelerate* at the same rate, not to move at the same constant speed.
problems.correction: This formula explains why a heavier object requires more force to accelerate at the same rate as a lighter one.
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates that force is needed to maintain speed; correction correctly links force to acceleration.

problems.quote: GLIMS integrated with ISRO ’s Resourcesat‑2A and Cartosat‑3 provides near‑real‑time lake‑area alerts
problems.problem: GLIMS is a global glacier inventory, not an operational near‑real‑time alert system; ISRO operates its own lake‑monitoring system.
problems.correction: ISRO’s Resourcesat‑2A and Cartosat‑3 provide near‑real‑time lake‑area alerts
problems.verifierReason: GLIMS is not a near‑real‑time lake‑alert system; ISRO’s Resourcesat‑2A and Cartosat‑3 provide such alerts.
Original calculation rounds incorrectly; correct division yields ~99,922, not 100,000.

problems.problem: The division algorithm states that the remainder r satisfies 0 ≤ r < b, but the text writes "0 ≤ r b" missing the '<' symbol.
problems.verifierReason: Original '0 ≤ r b' misses '<' operator; correction '0 ≤ r < b' matches Euclidean division theorem.

problems.quote: The exponent φ(n) is the order of the multiplicative group modulo n.
problems.problem: Confuses exponent of a group with its order; φ(n) is the order (size) of the multiplicative group, while the exponent is the least common multiple of element orders, given by Carmichael function λ(n).
problems.correction: φ(n) is the order of the multiplicative group modulo n.
problems.verifierReason: Original mislabels φ(n) as exponent; correction states φ(n) is the order, which is accurate.

problems.problem: The IR Code establishes a "Worker Re-skilling Fund", not a "rehabilitation fund".
problems.verifierReason: IR Code s.83 creates Worker Re-skilling Fund; no 'rehabilitation fund' exists.

problems.problem: Section 72 is "Application for permission for closure"; there is no separate "voluntary closure" fast-track. The Code mandates a 60-day decision period, not 30 days.
problems.correction: closure application under Section 72, decided within 60 days
problems.verifierReason: s.72 is closure application; s.73 mandates 60-day decision, not 30-day fast-track.

problems.problem: The appropriate government has 60 days to decide on a closure application under Section 73, not 30 days.
problems.verifierReason: s.73 gives appropriate government 60 days to decide closure application.

problems.quote: recommended by the National Commission on Labour (2002)
problems.problem: The National Commission on Labour (2002) did not recommend a 30-day fast-track closure route; this attribution is invented.
problems.verifierReason: Second NCL (2002) did not recommend a 30-day fast-track closure route.

problems.quote: Workmen of Hindustan Lever Ltd. v. Management (2020)
problems.problem: No such Supreme Court judgment exists in 2020; closure principles derive from earlier cases under the Industrial Disputes Act.
problems.verifierReason: No SC judgment 'Workmen of Hindustan Lever Ltd. v. Management (2020)' exists; leading case is 1996.

problems.quote: The Court also mandated that the rehabilitation fund be operationalised within six months of the Code's commencement
problems.problem: The IR Code provides a Worker Re-skilling Fund, not a rehabilitation fund, and the Code was not in force in 2020 for the Court to mandate its operationalisation.
problems.correction: The IR Code provides for a Worker Re-skilling Fund; no Supreme Court mandate exists.
problems.verifierReason: IR Code has Worker Re-skilling Fund, not rehabilitation fund; Code not in force in 2020 for SC mandate.

problems.quote: five members nominated from organisations representing gig and platform workers
problems.problem: The Central Board also includes five representatives of aggregators, which are omitted.
problems.correction: five representatives of aggregators and five representatives of gig and platform workers
problems.verifierReason: s.114 Central Board includes 5 aggregator reps and 5 gig/platform worker reps; quote omits aggregators.

problems.quote: determining contribution rates from aggregators (1‑2 % of turnover) and from workers (voluntary contributions)
problems.problem: The Central Board does not determine contribution rates; the Central Government notifies aggregator rates (capped at 2% of turnover), and worker contributions are voluntary but not set by the Board.
problems.correction: recommending contribution rates; the Central Government notifies aggregator rates up to 2% of turnover
problems.verifierReason: Central Board recommends rates; Central Govt notifies aggregator rates capped at 2% turnover.

problems.quote: Accountability mechanisms are embedded in Sections 115‑117
problems.problem: Grievance redressal (Section 118) and Ombudsman (Section 119) are not covered by Sections 115‑117.
problems.correction: Accountability mechanisms are embedded in Sections 115‑119
problems.verifierReason: Accountability includes grievance redressal (s.118) and Ombudsman (s.119), beyond s.115-117.

problems.quote: the 1‑2 % turnover contribution is a floor, not a ceiling
problems.problem: The Code caps aggregator contribution at 2%, making it a ceiling; no Delhi High Court judgment (Gig Workers' Association v. Union of India, 2023) exists that holds otherwise.
problems.correction: The Code sets a 2% ceiling on aggregator contributions; no such judgment exists.
problems.verifierReason: s.115(3) caps aggregator contribution at 2% turnover (ceiling); no Delhi HC 2023 judgment exists.
